checks.detail: runs_agent_code — test.sh executes agent's scene.py under strace+su agent; scoring reads only static artifacts.
uv.lock found in environment/workspace/ alongside pyproject.toml.
Dockerfile uses uv (COPY --from=ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:latest) with uv sync --no-install-project.
docker_image is set in task.toml pointing to us-west1-docker.pkg.dev registry.
Clear deliverable (output.mp4 via scene.py), explicit constraints (algorithmic MoviePy, no hardcoded per-frame data), and unambiguous success criterion.
Line 7 explicitly states 'your sandbox times out in 2 hours'.
Conversational colleague-handoff tone, concise and direct.
12 lines, well under the 100-line limit.
No scoring, reward, verifier, or evaluation terms found in any agent-visible files.
Pre-installed tools listed, run command documented, and starter scene.py provides working skeleton.
Default scene.py produces a solid black video which scores 0.0 due to SSIM gating at 0.70 against a non-trivial reference animation.
Clean-room restore from pristine tarball, source-level anti-cheat grep, user separation, strace containment, and /logs/verifier lockdown collectively block all validated attack vectors.
Agent runs as non-root user via `su agent -c` in test.sh line 51 with `user = "agent"` in task.toml.
Agent code execution is wrapped in `strace -f` with `timeout 300` (test.sh lines 48-51), blocking until all forked children exit.
Scoring script runs from /tests/ using /tests/.venv/bin/python, never imports from /app, and only reads the copied agent video and verified source snapshot.
All crash paths use fail_with() which writes reward 0.0 and exits 0; strace and scorer commands have explicit timeouts (300s and 600s respectively).
Baseline black video has duration ratio 0.15 (hard fail <0.75) and SSIM far below 0.70 gate, so score=0.0 via multiplicative zeroing.
SSIM, pHash, and duration metrics measure rendered video quality against reference, not the algorithmic approach; anti-cheat gates use generous 5x margins with floors.
Multiplicative aggregation prevents gaming any single easy dimension (duration is easiest but contributes zero if SSIM or pHash fail).
Empty/black/random videos fail the SSIM 0.70 gate; reference video is excluded from pristine restore and source-level grep blocks file I/O; data-dump approaches blocked by literal/array/string gates.
compute_reward.py accepts CLI args for agent video and source paths, reads saved artifacts, and can be re-run independently without agent execution.
All code paths (fail_reward, gate failures, normal scoring) write valid reward.json with score, subscores list, and optional additional_data; reward.txt always written.
Verifier scores SSIM, pHash, and duration — all inferable from the instruction to match reference.mp4; anti-cheat gates align with the instruction's ban on hardcoded per-frame data.
All key terms (MoviePy primitives, algorithmic approaches, self-contained) are defined or exemplified in instruction.md.
All tools listed in instruction.md (moviepy, pillow, opencv, scikit-image, numpy, ffmpeg, ffprobe, uv) are installed and verified by oracle tool checks (9/9 passed).
solution/solve.sh (32 lines) and solution/scene.py (58 lines) both exist and are non-empty.
Oracle scores 1.0 on both local (docker) and Modal with all tool checks passing (9/9, 0 failures).
No hidden tests; verification uses standard video similarity metrics (SSIM, pHash, duration) against the reference video the agent can see.
Slim base, apt cache cleaned, every package justified (git/tmux/strace for Harbor, ffmpeg/libgl1/libglib2.0-0 for moviepy+opencv).
Only solve.sh (with toolchain validation) and scene.py (identical to source_scene.py, expected overlap).

reward_design.formula_explanation: Multiplicative gating ensures all three visual similarity factors must be high for a non-trivial score, preventing gaming of any single dimension.

components.name: gated_ssim
components.metric: RGB SSIM averaged over 60 sampled frames with temporal offset search, gated at 0.70 with cubic scaling

components.name: phash_similarity
components.metric: Per-frame perceptual hash (pHash) Hamming distance normalized to [0,1]

components.name: duration_penalty
components.metric: Frame count ratio between agent and reference video
components.gate: hard fail outside [0.75, 1.25] ratio, linear ramp within

dimension_analysis.name: gated_ssim
dimension_analysis.notes: Requires actual pixel-level visual similarity above 0.70 gate with cubic scaling making near-perfect match needed for high scores

dimension_analysis.name: phash_similarity
dimension_analysis.notes: Perceptual hash catches structural/layout differences; correlated with SSIM but independently validates visual structure

dimension_analysis.name: duration_penalty
dimension_analysis.notes: Matching frame count is straightforward but cannot carry score alone due to multiplicative aggregation
